title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'magasins'. A magasin is a set M of 'figures' with two order relations: ≤ (being a face or closed sub-figure) and ≪ (lying in the closure or 'umbra'), satisfying Mag 1 (X≤Y ⇒ X≪Y) and Mag 2 (for X≪Y, the set {Y'≤Y | X≪Y'} has a least element). It also carries disjointness relations: ∥ ('disjoint') and |0| (read here as 'disjoint interiors'). The lieux L are the ≪-minimal elements, the 'points'. umb(X) is the set of lieux x≪X. Its interior part is umb(X)° = umb(X) − umb(∂X), where ∂X is the set of proper faces of X. MagL1 says every figure has a nonempty interior shadow.

This page adds MagL2': if every interior point of X is disjoint (∥) from every interior point of Y, then X|0|Y. By Mag 3 the converse implication already holds, so under MagL2 the relation |0| on M is completely determined by ∥ on points. Grothendieck observes that in all practical cases MagL1 implies MagL2, so MagL2 looks like the most useful axiom.

Proposition-Scholie: a 'strictly divisible' coarse magasin structure on M (one satisfying MagL2) is equivalent to the following data:
- relations ≤ and ≪ satisfying Mag 1, Mag 2 and MagL1;
- a relation ∥ on L only, subject to Mag div 3 (∥ is symmetric and antireflexive) and Mag div 4 (if Y≠Z are both faces of X, then every interior point of Y is ∥ to every interior point of Z).
Mag div 4 is the familiar cell-complex axiom that distinct faces of a cell have disjoint open cells.

Proof sketch: define |0| on M by the MagL2 condition, then check Mag 3 and Mag 4; the converse direction is immediate. The marginal note corrects one point: antireflexivity of the induced |0| needs umb(X)° ≠ ∅, i.e. MagL1.

The next page specializes to the 'quasi-ensembliste' case (distinct points are always disjoint). There the structure reduces to the pair (≤, ≪) alone.

Purpose: reduce the combinatorial 'tame topology' structure of a magasin to minimal data, namely two orders on figures plus a disjointness relation on points. This is a combinatorial analogue of describing a regular cell or stratified decomposition by its face poset, its closure relation and point-set disjointness.
errors: MagL2 only gives one direction (pointwise disjointness of interiors ⇒ |0|); the equivalence also uses Mag 3 from the previous page.

As the marginal note says, without MagL1 the induced |0| need not be antireflexive (if umb(X)° = ∅ the condition holds vacuously for X|0|X). So MagL1 is genuinely needed in the Scholie and is added as an inserted correction.
Naming is inconsistent: the axiom is introduced as MagL2' but then cited as MagL2.

ideas.what: Determining the 'disjoint interiors' relation on figures from a disjointness relation on points via interior shadows (MagL2)
ideas.modern_name: reconstruction of incidence/disjointness of a stratified or cell decomposition from points and open strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (cell complexes, face posets; Alexandrov-type finite topologies)
ideas.where_published: Analysis situs notes unpublished (only alluded to in Récoltes et Semailles / Esquisse regarding 'topologie modérée')

ideas.what: Scholie: a strictly divisible magasin is equivalent to (≤, ≪) satisfying Mag1, Mag2, MagL1 plus a symmetric antireflexive relation on points in which distinct faces have disjoint interiors
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic face-poset/closure-poset description of regular stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct analogue; closest are abstract cell complexes (Tucker, Kovalevsky) and closure posets of stratifications

missed.claim: Part of Grothendieck's unpublished combinatorial axiomatics of 'magasins' for tame topology: the reduction of the magasin structure to two order relations plus a point-disjointness relation. The terminology and axiom system (Mag 1–4, MagL1–2, Mag div 3–4) appear nowhere in the literature, but the mathematical content is elementary bookkeeping.
missed.quote: Cela signifie donc que |0| sur M se déduit de la relation ∥ sur L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 program of an axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame topology). It could interest people working on combinatorial models of o-minimal or stratified spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: Unpublished and specific to Grothendieck's magasin axiomatics, but the result is a routine equivalence of axiom systems mirroring standard cell-complex facts.
transcription_corrections: 'omb(X)°' should be 'umb(X)°' (umbra), consistent with the previous page.
'Proposition - Solution' should read 'Proposition - Scholie' (as on the next page).
Marginal note at the bottom: '* mais pas forcément l'antiréflexivité, il faut umb(X)° ≠ ∅'.
The inserted phrase reads roughly 'structures de magasin grossières' on M.
